frameworks.name: Three Levers to Expand Local Business Revenue
frameworks.definition: A three-part framework for scaling single-location revenue: compress delivery (increase throughput per location), add distribution channels (saturate market across platforms), or replicate the model (open new locations).

claims.text: Reducing class duration from 45 to 30 minutes increases throughput by roughly 1.5x per facility by eliminating breaks and compressing peak-load delivery (Alex Hormozi, gym operation example). This applies to time-slot-constrained service businesses.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Removing breaks and compressing class length allows more cohorts per day without reducing availability.
bounded_by: Does not apply to services where duration is contractually guaranteed or quality-dependent
Does not apply when customer experience degradation results from compression

claims.text: Extending operating hours increases capacity utilization of a single location without capital expansion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: service businesses with fixed location capacity
bounded_by: Does not apply when staffing costs exceed incremental revenue

claims.text: For local businesses in A or B markets (population density >50k in 10-mile radius), a single channel is sufficient to reach $1M annual revenue. For C or D markets (<50k people in 10-mile radius), multiple channels are required because the addressable market is too small for single-channel saturation (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Market size determines whether a single channel can reach sufficient volume; below the threshold, you must use multiple distribution channels to saturate the available audience.
bounded_by: Does not apply to non-local businesses (SaaS, e-commerce, national brands)

claims.text: The three sequential expansion levers for single-location businesses are: (1) improve efficiency of existing location (compress sessions, extend hours), (2) add distribution channels (social media, paid media), (3) open new locations. Each lever must be exhausted before moving to the next because physical capacity is the binding constraint.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Physical location capacity (four walls) is the ultimate constraint; once saturated through operational efficiency and channel density, replication is the only scaling path.
bounded_by: Does not apply to remote/digital businesses without physical constraints

claims.text: A single location in a local service business is a $100M+ opportunity when the replicable unit model is mature. Founders often underestimate local business ceiling by conflating single-unit economics with scalability; the true opportunity is in duplicating and scaling the model across multiple locations (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Skepticism about single-location scale is a founder psychology error; the model scales multiplicatively across locations once unit economics are proven.
bounded_by: Assumes a replicable, systems-dependent model exists

claims.text: In geographic markets with limited population density, you cannot rely solely on the one-avatar-one-product-one-channel rule (standard for non-local businesses at <$1M revenue); local businesses must distribute across multiple channels to achieve market saturation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.speaker_term: the rule of one avatar, one product, one channel
claims.mechanism: Market size constraint forces multi-channel distribution; single channel cannot reach sufficient volume in small addressable markets.
bounded_by: Exception applies only to geography-constrained local businesses

examples.text: At Alex Hormozi's first gym, when attendance reached overcapacity, he reduced class duration from 45 minutes to 30 minutes, eliminated breaks between classes, and kept all other variables constant. This compressed scheduling delivered 1.5x more classes per day in the same facility, increasing overall member throughput without expanding the physical space. The speaker explicitly ties this to efficiency optimization before expansion.

practices.text: When facing capacity constraints in a single location, first attempt to increase throughput via operational efficiency: reduce session duration, eliminate breaks, extend operating hours. Only open a new location after exhausting these efficiency improvements.

Before expanding to multiple locations, saturate your geographic market across distribution channels (Instagram, X, YouTube, Facebook, TikTok). Test multiple channels to identify which ones resonate with your local avatar.
For local service businesses, validate that the single-location model is genuinely replicable (systems-dependent, not founder-dependent) before scaling to multiple locations.
